criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a CSV/XLSX file with recruiter interactions, when I upload it, then the data is ingested into the system.
Given an invalid file format, when I attempt to upload, then I receive an error message.
Trust: Data ingestion is logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Persistence (SQLite via Sequelize) and audit logging added on top of the existing schema/parser/validator work. Ingestion now persists directly (IngestionBatch + RecruiterInteractionRecord) rather than deferring to a normalization stage, since none exists yet and STORY-002 needs the data to survive across requests — documented as a deliberate amendment in directives/vendor_ingestion_stage.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Idempotency dedup key is the uploaded file's SHA-256 hash (translated from CLAUDE.md's vendor_id/source/file_hash convention, which doesn't map to this recruiter-interaction schema). Every outcome (success, duplicate, rejected) writes an IngestionAuditLog row with a per-request correlationId echoed back in the HTTP response. 47/47 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given a job seeker is logged in, when they navigate to the dashboard, then they see a list of recruiter interactions.
Given a job seeker clicks on a recruiter interaction, when they view the details, then it loads within three clicks.
Trust: Every interaction detail view is logged with a timestamp.

stories.notes: Added the backend's first runnable entry point (backend/src/index.ts) since STORY-001 built the ingestion pipeline but never wired it into an app. Dashboard is server-rendered HTML (GET /dashboard, GET /dashboard/interactions/:id) reading the existing RecruiterInteractionRecord model via a new read-only service (recruiterInteractionsService) — no new frontend toolchain. All interpolated recruiter-supplied fields (name, company, notes) are HTML-escaped; verified live that an injected <script> tag renders inert. Dashboard-to-detail navigation is 1 click, inside the 3-click budget. Every successful detail fetch writes an InteractionViewLog row (interactionId + viewedAt), including repeat views; a 404 writes nothing. Failure paths covered: list/detail service errors render a 500 error page instead of crashing, unknown id renders 404, malformed id renders 400 — all with tests. Known gap, called out and accepted with the user before building: there is no auth system yet in this codebase (no story for one in r0), so 'job seeker is logged in' is satisfied as a single implicit job seeker rather than real login — revisit once an auth story exists. 63/63 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given a set of recruiter interaction data, when I manually review the data, then I can confirm the data is accurately attributed to the correct recruiter.
Given a data entry with incorrect attribution, when I identify and correct it, then the system updates the attribution correctly.
Trust: Every manual correction is logged with the reviewer ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Built as a data-reviewer-facing manual review interface, per the story narrative and STORY-000's owner list ('Data Reviewer' owns STORY-003) rather than REQ-004's literal 'job seekers' wording, which appears to be a mismatched requirement -- flagged to the user and confirmed rather than silently building around it; REQ-004's text should be corrected to say 'data reviewer' to match. No auth system exists (same gap as STORY-002's implicit job seeker), so reviewer identity is captured as a required free-text reviewer ID field on the review form itself rather than a login -- deliberately not stubbed with a placeholder, since REQ-007 is a SAFE requirement and a fake ID would make the Trust criterion trivially true. New AttributionReview log records every review action (confirmed or corrected) with reviewerId, previous/new recruiter name+company, and a timestamp; confirming is treated as a real review event and logged too, not just corrections, since a reviewer confirming correct attribution is itself the manual-review action REQ-004/REQ-010 ask for. Attribution update + log write share one transaction. Failure paths covered with tests: missing reviewer ID and empty recruiter name re-render the form with the error and preserve what the reviewer typed rather than losing it, unknown/malformed interaction id, and save failures (mocked service rejection) all leave the underlying record untouched. Verified live end-to-end against an isolated server/database (not reusing the developer's running instance): uploaded data, opened the review form, submitted a correction, confirmed it applied and redirected, and confirmed the missing-reviewer-ID path leaves the record unchanged. 78/78 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given ingested data, when red flags are identified, then they are highlighted on the dashboard.
Given no red flags, when I view the dashboard, then no highlights are shown.
Trust: Red flag identification is logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Four fixed, factual, versioned red-flag rules (payment/personal-data phrases in notes, personal email domain while a company is named, same email under different companies, offer with no earlier interview), worked out when the data is read and highlighted 'for review' without hiding anything or scoring recruiters (REQ-015); each identification is logged once to red_flag_logs, a failed check shows a 'check unavailable' notice, and if only the audit write fails the flags still show and are logged on the next load. Known limits: phrase matching ignores negation ('no fee') and is English-only, company names aren't normalised beyond case and spacing, and R2 also flags legitimate independent recruiters who use personal email.

criteria.text: Given uncertain data, when it is flagged, then a data reviewer is notified for manual review.
Given certain data, when I view it, then no flag is shown.
Trust: Flagging actions are logged for audit purposes.

stories.notes: Four fixed, factual, versioned rules flag uncertain data (recruiter can't be identified, dated after submission, possible duplicate across uploads, one email under different names); flagged data is held in 'Waiting for review' with its evidence, never judged or rejected (REQ-005), and a data reviewer is notified via GET /api/history-review/notifications and the review queue. Each flag is recorded once in uncertain_data_flags (the notification and the audit entry). Fail-safe: if the check cannot run, attested data with no ruling is held rather than confirmed, rulings pause (503), recorded notifications keep showing, and the dashboard shows a notice. Known limits: checks rescan the whole table on each read; name-spelling variants under one email are flagged for a reviewer to decide.

stories.notes: Reviewers never edit submitted data: a reviewer (or rule U1, automatically) raises a correction request; the job seeker answers with an attested correction, confirmation or 'unavailable', stored as a new version with the original kept; the reviewer's ruling closes it. Each action is logged with actor and time. Known limits: actor IDs are typed in (no login yet), and STORY-003's edit form still overwrites the stored row; a later correction to the same field displays over it, and STORY-016 removes that form.

criteria.text: Given a dataset for ingestion, when I run the cleaning process, then the system removes or corrects invalid data entries.
Given a dataset with missing fields, when I run the cleaning process, then the system flags entries with missing fields for review.
Trust: Every cleaning action is logged with the administrator ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Built as its own admin-run pre-ingestion stage -- POST /api/vendor-ingestion/clean -- rather than folding silently into STORY-001's /upload, since the acceptance criteria describe cleaning as an explicit action ('when I run the cleaning process') and invalid rows there were previously just dropped and reported as a string, never corrected or held for review. administratorId is a required free-text form field (same precedent as STORY-002/003: no auth system exists yet, and REQ-014 being SAFE means a placeholder ID would make the Trust criterion trivially true). Classifier (dataCleaningService.cleanRow/cleanRows) treats recruiterName and interactionDate as the required fields for flagging (interactionType has a schema default so is never 'missing'); a row is corrected (whitespace trim, email case/format normalization, dropping an unusably malformed optional email) and kept whenever safely fixable, flagged and kept when a required field is simply absent, and only removed outright when a required field is present but unparseable (e.g. a garbage interactionDate) -- there is no safe way to guess it. Every action (corrected/flagged_for_review/removed) is persisted to the new DataCleaningLog table with administratorId, rowNumber, field, detail, and a cleanedAt timestamp; a run with nothing to fix logs nothing, since there is no action to log. Required extracting the raw-row parsing step out of STORY-001's vendorIngestionCsvParser.ts/vendorIngestionXlsxParser.ts into parseRecruiterInteractionsCsvRows/XlsxRows, because those files previously parsed straight into schema validation and never exposed field-level raw data for cleaning to act on -- purely an extraction, existing parseRecruiterInteractionsCsv/Xlsx exports and their test suites are unchanged and still pass. This route does not itself persist rows into the ingestion tables; it is a pre-ingestion gate/report, and the administrator re-submits the cleaned file through the existing /upload endpoint. Failure paths covered with tests: missing administratorId (400, nothing logged), unsupported file extension, and the unparseable-date removal path. Verified live end-to-end against an isolated server and SQLite database (not the developer's running instance): ran a real CSV with one clean row, one correctable email-casing row, one missing-recruiterName row, and one unparseable-date row through the real endpoint, and confirmed the response counts and the persisted DataCleaningLog rows (administratorId + cleanedAt) directly against the database file. 89/89 backend tests passing; tsc --noEmit clean.

criteria.text: Given a job seeker uploads recruiter interaction data, when they submit the file, then the system requires them to attest the data is factual before any row is accepted.
Given an interaction that was never attested or is later disputed, when it exists in the system, then it is routed to manual review instead of being treated as confirmed recruiter history.
Trust: every attestation is logged against its submission with a timestamp.

stories.notes: Upload (POST /api/vendor-ingestion/upload) now requires attested=true + attestedBy; the attestation is stored in the same transaction as its batch (statement, channel, timestamp) and a missing one is rejected and logged with no rows stored. History status is computed on read from attestations, disputes and reviewer decisions (open dispute > reviewer ruling > attestation); unattested (incl. all pre-STORY-015 rows) and disputed interactions go to a reviewer queue at /api/history-review and are kept out of confirmed history on the dashboard and /api/interactions. Review writes are serialised in-process because Sequelize's sqlite driver errors on overlapping transactions. 'Upload' is read as any job-seeker submission: channel 'file' now, 'form' reserved. 148/148 backend tests passing; verified live against a copy of the dev database.

criteria.text: Given an interaction with incorrect attribution, when I identify it during review, then I can request a correction from the job seeker with a reason, and I cannot change the attribution myself.

Given an attribution correction request, when the job seeker responds, by correcting the recruiter name or company, confirming the original is correct, or stating the information is unavailable, with a reason in each case, then the system records the response (any correction as a new attested version, with the original kept) and returns the interaction for review.
Trust: Every request, response and review decision is logged with the actor's ID and timestamp.
